source.objectiveEnglish: Say who does each task on site using regular present-tense verbs.
source.focusSpanish: Present-tense -ar, -er, -ir endings for yo, tú, usted, nosotros and ellos
source.speakingEnglish: Split today's tasks with a coworker: say who cuts, who carries the blocks up and who cleans the site.

archivedDraft.title: Where work happens
archivedDraft.scene: Later that morning, Sato asks Tanaka where Kobayashi is, where each worker will carry out tasks, and where Sato's saw is kept
materialDrift: Older Japanese Foundation 6 teaches location particles with Sato and Tanaka; source Foundation 6 divides Carlos and Ana's cutting, carrying, mixing and cleanup tasks.

cards.sourceNoteInternal: Common in Mexico and the US; some say el sheetrock.
tú is fine between coworkers; -ar: corto, cortas, corta.

cards.sourceSpanish: Nosotros limpiamos la obra a las 4.
cards.japaneseDraft: 私たちは4時に現場を清掃します。

cards.sourceSpanish: Ellos suben los bloques al segundo piso.
cards.sourceEnglish: They carry the blocks up to the second floor.
cards.sourceNoteInternal: -ir verb: subo, subes, sube, subimos, suben.
cards.japaneseDraft: あの人たちはブロックを2階へ運び上げます。

cards.sourceSpanish: Yo barro y ellos recogen la basura.
cards.sourceEnglish: I sweep and they pick up the trash.
cards.sourceNoteInternal: -er verbs: barro, barres, barre, barremos, barren.
cards.japaneseDraft: 私は掃き掃除をし、あの人たちはごみを拾います。

cards.sourceSpanish: Tú mezclas la arena con el cemento.
cards.sourceEnglish: You mix the sand with the cement.
cards.japaneseDraft: 砂とセメントを混ぜます。

reader.sourceSpanish: Carlos divide las tareas con Ana en la obra.
reader.sourceEnglish: Carlos splits the tasks with Ana at the site.
reader.japaneseDraft: カルロスは現場でアナと作業を分担します。

reader.sourceSpanish: Carlos: Yo corto la tablaroca con la sierra.
reader.sourceEnglish: Carlos: I cut the drywall with the saw.
reader.japaneseDraft: カルロス：「私はのこぎりで石膏ボードを切ります。」

reader.sourceSpanish: Ana: Yo pongo los tornillos en la tablaroca.
reader.sourceEnglish: Ana: I put the screws in the drywall.

reader.sourceSpanish: Ana: Yo reviso la pared con el nivel.
reader.sourceEnglish: Ana: I check the wall with the level.
reader.japaneseDraft: アナ：「私は水準器で壁を確認します。」

reader.sourceSpanish: Carlos: Luis y Pedro suben los bloques al segundo piso.
reader.sourceEnglish: Carlos: Luis and Pedro carry the blocks up to the second floor.
reader.japaneseDraft: カルロス：「ルイスとペドロはブロックを2階へ運び上げます。」

reader.sourceSpanish: Carlos: Tú mezclas la arena y la grava con el cemento.
reader.sourceEnglish: Carlos: You mix the sand and the gravel with the cement.
reader.japaneseDraft: カルロス：「砂と砂利をセメントと混ぜます。」

reader.sourceSpanish: Carlos: Nosotros limpiamos la obra a las 4.
reader.sourceEnglish: Carlos: We clean the site at 4.
reader.japaneseDraft: カルロス：「私たちは4時に現場を清掃します。」

reader.sourceSpanish: Carlos: Yo barro y ellos recogen la basura.
reader.sourceEnglish: Carlos: I sweep and they pick up the trash.
reader.japaneseDraft: カルロス：「私は掃き掃除をし、あの人たちはごみを拾います。」

reader.sourceSpanish: Ana: Yo lavo la cubeta con la manguera.
reader.sourceEnglish: Ana: I wash the bucket with the hose.
reader.japaneseDraft: アナ：「私はホースでバケツを洗います。」

decisionsNeeded: Choose a Japanese task and register contrast that preserves the source's tú versus usted focus without pretending Japanese has Spanish person endings; card 13 remains null.
Resolve whether Reader 3 puts, drives or fastens screws into drywall before selecting Japanese construction wording.
Review tablaroca/drywall, wall checking with a level, block carry to the second floor, mixing sand/gravel/cement and cleanup vocabulary with qualified Japanese and trade specialists.
Keep the source's four-o'clock schedule and Carlos, Ana, Luis and Pedro roles exact; do not use the older Sato/Tanaka location scene or its audio.
Author six actual mode prompt/target pairs, forms, speaking, contextual dictionary and saved-item mapping before learner use.
